en.name: Tapenade
en.summary: A jar of tapenade keeps 9 months from purchase, in the cupboard or the refrigerator. Refrigeration is not necessary for a commercial jar — the salt, acid and oil do the work — but it is worth doing because the flavour improves in the cold.
en.pantry: Cool, dark and dry, 9 months from purchase. Commercial tapenade is olives, capers, oil and usually anchovy and lemon or vinegar: a salty, acidic, oil-covered paste, and that combination is why it sits on a shelf rather than in the chiller. Keep the paste level and covered by its own oil, top it up with a film of olive oil if it dries out, and always use a clean dry spoon. A home-made tapenade is a different proposition — it has no controlled acidity and should be treated as a fresh dip and refrigerated.
en.fridge: Refrigerating at 4 °C (40 °F) or below also gives 9 months, so the choice is not about extending the life: refrigeration is not necessary, but the flavour improves. Cold firms the paste and lets the olive, caper and anchovy flavours settle together; take the jar out a quarter of an hour before serving so the oil clears and the paste spreads. Once opened, the fridge is still the better habit in a warm kitchen, simply because it slows the oil going stale.
en.freezer: No freezer timeline is published for tapenade. Freezing it is not harmful and works better than for most oily preparations, because the paste is already coarse — but the oil separates and goes slightly waxy on thawing, and it needs a hard stir to come back. With 9 months available either way, the freezer is rarely the answer. If you do freeze it, use small portions in an ice cube tray rather than the whole jar.
en.thawing: Thaw in the fridge and stir the separated oil back in before serving. Do not refreeze it.
spoilage: A rancid or crayon-like smell from oil that has oxidised.
Mould on the surface, usually where the paste was not covered by oil.
Fizzing, bubbling or a fermented smell when the jar is opened.
A dried, darkened crust with liquid separating underneath.
tips: Keep a film of olive oil over the surface to stop it drying and darkening.
Use a clean dry spoon; never double-dip from a cracker.
Take it out of the fridge a quarter of an hour before serving.
Treat home-made tapenade as a fresh dip and refrigerate it.

faq.a: 9 months from purchase, in a cool cupboard or refrigerated at 4 °C (40 °F) or below.

faq.q: Does tapenade need to be refrigerated?
faq.a: A commercial jar does not — the salt, acid and oil preserve it. Refrigerating is worth doing for flavour, and home-made tapenade should always be kept cold.

faq.q: Why has the oil separated on top?
faq.a: That is normal for an olive paste and is not spoilage. Stir it back in, and keep a film of oil over the surface to protect it.

zh.name: 橄欖醬（tapenade）
zh.summary: 市售橄欖醬從購買日起算可放 9 個月，放櫥櫃或冷藏都一樣。市售罐裝其實不需要冷藏——鹽、酸與油已經完成工作——但冰過值得做，因為風味會更融合。
zh.pantry: 陰涼、避光、乾燥，自購買日起 9 個月。市售 tapenade 是橄欖、酸豆、橄欖油，通常還有鯷魚與檸檬或醋：一份又鹹又酸、表面被油覆蓋的醬泥，這個組合就是它能待在常溫貨架而不是冷藏櫃的原因。請保持表面平整並被自己的油蓋住，乾掉的話補一層橄欖油，也一律使用乾淨乾燥的湯匙。自家做的橄欖醬則是另一回事：它的酸度沒有經過控制，應該當成新鮮沾醬處理並冷藏。
zh.fridge: 冷藏在 4 °C 以下同樣是 9 個月，所以選擇冷藏並不是為了延長期限：冷藏並非必要，但風味會更好。低溫讓醬體變得緊實，也讓橄欖、酸豆與鯷魚的味道彼此沉澱融合；上桌前提早一刻鐘拿出來，油會恢復清澈、醬也比較好抹。開封之後，在溫暖的廚房裡冷藏仍然是更好的習慣，因為它能拖慢油脂走味。
zh.freezer: 橄欖醬沒有公布的冷凍期限。冷凍不會有害，效果也比大多數含油醬料好，因為它本來就是粗顆粒的醬泥——但解凍後油會分離、略帶蠟感，需要用力攪回去。既然兩邊都有 9 個月可用，冷凍很少是答案。真的要冷凍，請用製冰盒分小份，而不是整罐下去。
zh.thawing: 放冷藏解凍，上桌前把分離的油攪回去。不要二次冷凍。
spoilage: 油氧化後發出油耗味或蠟筆味。
表面長霉，通常在沒有被油蓋住的地方。
開罐時冒泡、起氣或有發酵味。
表面結出變深的乾殼，底下滲出液體。
tips: 表面保持一層橄欖油，防止變乾變黑。
用乾淨乾燥的湯匙，不要用餅乾直接挖第二次。
上桌前一刻鐘從冰箱拿出來。
自製橄欖醬當新鮮沾醬處理，一定要冷藏。

faq.a: 自購買日起 9 個月，放陰涼櫥櫃或冷藏 4 °C 以下都一樣。
市售罐裝不需要，鹽、酸與油就是它的保存系統。冰過是為了風味；自製的則一定要冷藏。

faq.q: 上面浮一層油是壞了嗎？
faq.a: 不是，橄欖醬出油很正常。攪回去即可，並在表面保留一層油保護它。
